best_prompt: Output exactly one candidate by default. Only produce multiple candidates (2–3) if and only if the integrator guarantees an external CLIP reranker. When multiple candidates are allowed, produce up to three deterministic variants created only by changing the Line 1 tag set or by selecting alternate CLIP-preferred surface synonyms for the same canonical_id(s); do not introduce free-form wording differences. Each candidate must be exactly two lines (Line 1 = comma-separated tags; Line 2 = caption). Separate candidates with a single blank line. If you cannot produce a reliable candidate under the verifier's checks, output exactly: image unclear.
final_prompt:
Primary objective
- MAXIMIZE CLIP image–text similarity (primary). SigLIP is diagnostic only.

Operational summary (high-level)
- Deterministically generate up to 3 candidate captions for every image, normalize them with the exact CLIP normalizer, rerank using a CLIP reranker (external preferred; internal required if external unavailable). Only after full generation + normalization + reranking/fallback + acceptance/unit checks may the system return the exact lower-case token sequence:
image unclear

Hard-ordered step sequence (MUST be followed; single exception: catastrophic system failure)
1) GENERATE: deterministically produce the full set of candidate captions (up to 3 distinct candidates) for every image. Do NOT return "image unclear" before completing Steps 1–4.
2) NORMALIZE: run the exact CLIP tokenizer/normalizer on every generated string (document version). Use normalized strings for all comparisons, reranking inputs, and automated checks. Log original + normalized.
3) RERANK: rerank the normalized candidates with the CLIP reranker (external preferred). If external reranker unavailable, run the INTERNAL CLIP reranker. If no CLIP model exists at all, run the calibrated fallback heuristic and set reranker_absent = true in logs.
4) ACCEPTANCE/UNIT CHECKS: apply acceptance thresholds, margin logic, and unit tests to the top-ranked candidate. Only after Steps 1–4 fail may the system output "image unclear".

Output requirements (final outputs)
- If an acceptable candidate is found after Steps 1–4, return EXACTLY one final accepted candidate in two lines:
  Line 1: canonical tags, comma-separated, no trailing comma. Default exactly 3 tags (primary object, action token if included, one salient attribute). A deterministic 4th context tag (scene/secondary-object) is allowed ONLY when the "4th-tag" conditions (below) are met; if present, return 3 or 4 tags as used in the candidate.
  Line 2: one concise sentence ending with a single period.
- If, AFTER full generation + normalization + reranking/fallback + acceptance checks (with cosmetic-tolerant subject matching) NO candidate is acceptable, return EXACTLY and ONLY:
image unclear

Tokenization / normalization (MUST)
- Use the exact CLIP normalization/tokenization for all generation, internal checks, reranking input:
  - Unicode NFC, lowercase, collapse repeated whitespace to single space, normalize hyphens to ASCII hyphen, strip surrounding punctuation except a permitted terminal period, canonicalize diacritics.
- Record and log CLIP-normalizer version. Log both original and normalized strings. Cosmetic diffs are tolerated for subject matching but must be recorded.

Canonical vocabulary and per-surface-token validation (MUST at generation time)
- Integrator provides per-surface-token lists: keep, neutral, demote (from dev CLIP ablations).
  - Prefer keep tokens for each slot.
  - Use neutral tokens ONLY when no keep exists for a required slot; every neutral usage must be logged.
  - NEVER generate tokens marked demote.
- Do NOT block candidate generation if a keep verb is absent; include dev-validated neutral/fallback verbs as candidates instead.

Candidate format and composition (generation-first, deterministic)
- Candidate count: ALWAYS generate up to 3 deterministic, non-identical candidates. Determinism enforced by canonical priority lists and documented tie-breakers.
- Candidate diversity requirement: candidates must differ along at least two of these axes (prioritized): verb/frame (keep→neutral), attribute specificity (color→material→pattern/clothing), scene/context/secondary-object token, foreground/background role, primary-tag synonym. Document tie-breakers.
- Candidate per-candidate format during generation:
  Line 1 (tags): 3 tags by default, ordered:
    1) primary object token — REQUIRED and should be supported by detector_primary_tag_threshold if detector exists.
    2) action token — include only if action_detector_confidence ≥ action_inclusion_threshold AND token ∈ keep ∪ allowed-neutral (if no keep exists).
    3) one salient attribute token — exactly one of {color OR count OR position OR material/pattern/clothing}, chosen from keep ∪ neutral (neutral only when no keep exists).
  - Optional 4th context tag: allow a deterministic 4th tag (scene/secondary-object) only when BOTH:
    a) detector_confidence for that token ≥ high_confidence_threshold OR token is a dev-validated high-CLIP textual keeper, AND
    b) dev validation shows per-token CLIP benefit for adding this 4th tag. Log justification.
  - No synonyms/repeats within a candidate.
  Line 2 (caption sentence):
    - Must begin with Line1 primary tag's preferred surface token AFTER normalization (subject-first unless dev-validated alternative is better).
    - Sentence shape: [Subject] [verb/frame OR copula/none] [short relationship/object phrase (optional)] [single salient attribute phrase] [optional single context phrase].
    - Active verbs from CLIP-validated verb-list (keep preferred; neutral/fallback allowed when no keep). Verbs are OPTIONAL: noun-centric or copula constructions permitted when they better match the visual content.
    - INCLUDE the exact attribute token from Line1; may reuse the 4th context tag if present.
    - Target token length: 12–18 tokens. Hard max 20 tokens. Shorter permitted only when constraints satisfied and subject/attribute fidelity preserved.
    - Allow at most one appositive comma or one short prepositional phrase to add high-value discriminative detail (e.g., age/clothing/location). No lists, no subordinate clauses, no speculative language. End with a single period.
    - No repeated attributes or multi-attribute lists separated by commas.

Determinism and candidate diversity (MUST)
- Candidate generation MUST be deterministic across runs for the same inputs. Use canonical priority lists and explicit tie-breakers.
- If fewer than 3 distinct candidates are possible under constraints, still produce the distinct set (1–3) and proceed to reranking.

Reranking and fallback (MUST-run)
- RERANK all normalized candidates with CLIP and choose the highest-scoring candidate.
- If external reranker unavailable, an INTERNAL CLIP reranker is REQUIRED. If truly no CLIP model exists, use the calibrated fallback heuristic (below) and set reranker_absent = true and log heuristic values.
- Reranker MUST receive normalized strings.

No-reranker calibrated fallback heuristic (ONLY when no CLIP reranker exists)
- Score = w1 * TagPrecisionScore + w2 * RerankMarginProxy - w3 * LengthPenalty - w4 * SubjectMismatchPenalty
  - Emphasize TagPrecisionScore and RerankMarginProxy; penalize substantive subject mismatches heavily.
  - LengthPenalty = max(0, token_count - 18) (reflects new length regime).
  - SubjectMismatchPenalty = 0 for cosmetic-normalization-only diffs; = 1 for substantive mismatches.
  - RerankMarginProxy = normalized(best_tag_precision - second_best_tag_precision).
- Integrator must tune weights on dev and log calibration results.

TagPrecisionScore and grounding (MUST)
- TagPrecisionScore must prioritize specific, discriminative nouns and attributes (clothing, object parts, scene elements) and penalize overly-generic tokens ("person", "thing") unless no better token exists.
- Incorporate per-token CLIP ablation contributions into TagPrecisionScore.
- Require detector top-1 for primary tag unless dev ablation shows a textual token provides a larger CLIP benefit. Substantive subject mismatches must be penalized heavily in fallback.

Acceptance thresholds and margin-based acceptance (MUST be tuned on dev)
- Default starting clip_threshold = 0.20. Integrator MUST sweep clip_threshold in [0.20, 0.24] and choose final value on dev.
- Acceptance rules:
  - If top_CLIP ≥ clip_threshold → ACCEPT (subject to unit/format checks).
  - If top_CLIP < clip_threshold: allow margin-based acceptance ONLY when BOTH:
    a) top_vs_next_margin ≥ margin_accept_threshold (tunable on dev), AND
    b) TagPrecisionScore ≥ tag_precision_threshold (tuned on dev).
  - If reranker_absent: use analogous checks against the heuristic score and a tuned heuristic_accept_threshold.
- All margin-accept decisions MUST be logged with per-example reasoning. Margin acceptance must be enabled only after dev evidence supports it.

Verifier / "image unclear" (conservative, post-generation)
- RETURN EXACTLY AND ONLY "image unclear" if ANY of these apply after full generation + reranking/fallback + unit/format checks:
  1) No primary object detected above detector_primary_tag_threshold AND no high-confidence alternate primary exists across generated candidates.
  2) After CLIP reranking: top candidate CLIP score < clip_threshold AND (top_vs_next_margin < margin_accept_threshold OR TagPrecisionScore insufficient). (If reranker absent: analogous using heuristic.)
  3) Any strict formatting/unit test fails after normalization and cosmetic-tolerant subject match: invalid tag set (demote token used), wrong tag count (unless justified 4th tag meets conditions), Line2 contains multiple attributes/lists/subordinate clauses, Line2 token_count > 20, or disallowed verb.
  4) Active-verb unavailability: no candidate contains a validated verb OR valid noun-centric/copy choices AND no dev-approved fallback exists.
- When returning "image unclear", output EXACTLY:
image unclear

Automated checks and unit tests (MUST run programmatically after reranking/fallback)
1) Whitelist/CLIP-preference check: every Line1 tag ∈ keep ∪ allowed-neutral-for-this-id (neutral usage logged).
2) Tag count/composition: default exactly 3 tags; 4th tag allowed only per validated rule and logged.
3) Subject reuse: normalized(Line2 subject) must match normalized(Line1 primary); cosmetic diffs allowed and logged.
4) Length: token_count(Line2) ≤ 20; prefer 12–18.
5) Punctuation: at most one appositive comma OR one short prepositional phrase; Line2 ends with a single period.
6) Verb presence: at least one candidate must contain a keep verb OR permitted neutral/fallback OR be an approved noun-centric frame; final verb/frame must be permitted per dev policy.
7) Grounding: detector confidences for included tags must meet thresholds unless neutral token usage explicitly allowed.
8) Tokenization-normalization: normalized strings must match CLIP normalizer exactly; log cosmetic diffs.
- If any automated checks fail after the full flow (other than cosmetic-normalization-only failures), return "image unclear". If failure is cosmetic-normalization-only, perform deterministic canonical rewrite using the exact CLIP normalizer and re-run checks once; if still failing, return "image unclear". Do NOT perform freeform rewrites beyond canonical normalization.

Telemetry, logging, and CI gating (MANDATORY)
- For every invocation, log:
  - All generated candidates (original + normalized), which tokens are keep/neutral/demote, candidate-level CLIP scores and margins, detector confidences, TagPrecisionScore, reranker_absent flag if set, final decision, and a single canonical failure reason if "image unclear".
  - Per-token average CLIP contribution (from dev) and per-example per-token CLIP deltas when reranker used.
- CI gating: Integrator MUST block deployment if dev validation sweep yields mean_delta_clip < 0 or clip_win_rate below agreed threshold. Run dev sweeps for clip_threshold, margin_accept_threshold, action/scene/primary thresholds, and heuristic weight tuning.

Dev calibration requirements (MUST before production)
- Build per-primary keep/neutral/demote token lists using per-surface CLIP ablations; lock keep tokens only when stable & positive.
- Run per-token CLIP ablation to compute average per-token contribution; use this to prune demote tokens and promote keep tokens.
- Tune clip_threshold, margin_accept_threshold, TagPrecisionScore weights, detector thresholds, high_confidence_threshold for 4th tag, and fallback heuristic weights to maximize mean_CLIP and mean_delta_clip on dev.
- Validate 4th-tag expansion rule on dev before enabling in production.

Practical generation guidance (deterministic + richer)
- Broaden candidate diversity axes: verb/frame, attribute specificity (color → material → pattern/clothing), scene/context token, secondary-object presence, foreground/background relation.
- Allow verbs to be optional; accept copula/passive/noun-centric frames when they better match image content.
- Permit at most one high-value comma or short prepositional phrase to include discriminative details (age, clothing, location). Avoid lists and subordinate clauses.

Quick implementation and dev-checklist (immediate enforcement)
- Enforce CLIP normalizer usage and version logging; add unit tests asserting normalization before reranking.
- Change target token length to 12–18 (hard max 20) and enforce with unit tests and CI.
- Allow deterministic 4th context tag under validated conditions; log justification.
- Expand keep lists with high-value nouns/attributes shown to improve CLIP on dev (e.g., sink, umbrella, bridge, stage, water, metal); validate by ablation.
- Re-run dev sweeps to pick clip_threshold ∈ [0.20,0.24], margin_accept_threshold, and TagPrecisionScore weights. Block release if mean_delta_clip < 0.

Final requirement restated
- Do NOT return "image unclear" before generating candidates and reranking/fallback.
- AFTER unconditional generation, normalization, reranking/fallback, margin consideration, and formatting/unit checks (with cosmetic-tolerant subject matching and a single normalization-only deterministic rewrite attempt), if no acceptable candidate remains, output EXACTLY and ONLY:
image unclear

best_record.old_prompt:
Output exactly one candidate by default. Only produce 2–3 alternate candidates if and only if an external CLIP reranker is guaranteed by the integrator; when multiple candidates are produced, separate each candidate by a single blank line. Each candidate must be exactly two lines (Line 1 = tags; Line 2 = caption). If you cannot produce a reliable caption under the checks below, output exactly:
image unclear

Line 1 — tags (required)
- Format: 2–3 comma-separated lower-case tokens (prefer exactly 3 when at least three high-confidence nouns exist). No punctuation except commas. No extra whitespace beyond single spaces around commas.
- Token types: visible concrete noun(s) or a single visible adjective token as the only attribute token. Multiword fused objects (e.g., "traffic light", "wine bottle") count as one token.
- Canonicalization required: every tag must have an upstream canonical_id from the canonical inventory (recommended: COCO/Visual Genome/CLIP-common). Before generating captions, map detector/classifier outputs to these canonical IDs. Normalize plurals→singular and synonyms→canonical_id.
- Ordering & deduplication: deduplicate tokens; sort tokens by score = 0.6 * detector_confidence + 0.4 * normalized_CLIP_retrieval_frequency, descending. If two detectors are within tie_break_delta_confidence (default 10%), prefer the noun with higher CLIP_retrieval_frequency.
- Attribute tokens: allow at most one adjective token (color/size). Include attribute token only if attribute_confidence ≥ attribute_confidence_threshold (default 70%). If below threshold, drop the attribute from Line 1 and Line 2.
- Forbidden tokens: no meta/tooling words, no proper nouns/brands, no identity-sensitive dates/events, no inferred identities or emotions. Scene/event nouns allowed only if a scene classifier gives high confidence and they map to canonical inventory.
- If fewer than two high-confidence specific nouns remain after filtering, do not invent tags. If at least one reliable noun exists, produce Line 1 with that noun (1–2 tokens) and follow the Option B fallback rules. If no reliable noun exists, leave Line 1 empty and output Line 2 = "image unclear".

Line 2 — caption (required)
- Two valid options. All checks below are hard constraints. If any check for Option A fails, immediately produce Option B (if allowed) or "image unclear" as specified.
- Global constraints for both options:
  - No punctuation except one optional trailing period on Option A only. No commas. Lower-case except canonical synonyms that require capitalization by canonical mapping (rare).
  - Do not introduce any new concrete noun, attribute, identity, emotion, or inferred action that does not map to a Line 1 canonical_id. Every non-function word in Line 2 must be traceable to a Line 1 token via identical string or canonical_id mapping. If this fails, reject and fallback.
  - The canonical main noun (Line 1 first token) must appear verbatim or as a canonical synonym (same canonical_id) in Line 2 and must appear early (within the first 3–4 tokens or in the subject phrase).
  - If you cannot verify canonical mapping for nouns in Line 2, reject and fallback.
- Option A (preferred when checks pass):
  - One factual sentence in present simple or present progressive (subject + verb + object/prepositional phrase).
  - Word count: exactly 7–13 words.
  - Verb requirement: exactly one clear visible verb (allowed verbs list: sits, stands, rides, holds, carries, walks, leans, looks, points, reads, opens, plays, wears, pushes, pulls, places, covers, is holding, is sitting, dances, performs, marches, runs, climbs, jumps, throws, catches, skates). OR exactly one concrete spatial preposition used as the single main relation (on, in, near, by, next to, in front of, behind).
  - Token overlap: must share at least two canonical tokens with Line 1 (one must be the main noun). If Line 1 contains only one token, Option A is allowed only if at least one other token in Line 2 maps to a Line 1 canonical_id (i.e., impossible → fallback).
  - No compound verbs, no additional predicates, no subordinate clauses, and no added objects/attributes beyond Line 1 canonical_ids.
  - Example pattern: "a child rides a red motorcycle down the street."
- Option B (fallback; use when fewer than two high-confidence nouns or when any Option A check fails):
  - Conservative phrase of exactly 2–4 tokens, pattern: "<main_noun> <preposition> <scene/location>" or "<main_noun> <scene>" (examples: "dog on sidewalk", "red car in street", "man near tree"). No verbs. No punctuation.
  - The main noun must be the Line 1 first token (or its canonical synonym).
  - Use Option B whenever fewer than two high-confidence nouns exist, or whenever Option A fails any hard check (word count, verb count, token_overlap, or new-noun introduction).
- If no valid Option B fallback can be constructed (no reliable noun), output exactly:
image unclear

Operational & tuning parameters (defaults & required logs)
- attribute_confidence_threshold = 70% (recommended sweep: 60, 70, 75).
- preferred_tag_count = 3 (use 2 only when fewer than 3 high-confidence nouns available).
- tie_break_delta_confidence = 10 percentage points.
- If external CLIP reranker is absent, produce exactly one candidate. If present, you may output up to 3 candidates derived from alternate high-confidence Line 1 sets (each candidate must individually pass the checks above).

Diagnostics (required per candidate; structured JSON-like log)
For every candidate generated, produce a compact diagnostics object (for tuning and reranking). Include:
{ 
  "candidate_id": string,
  "option_used": "A" or "B",
  "line1_tokens": [{ "text": "...", "canonical_id": "...", "detector_confidence": n, "clip_retrieval_freq": n }, ...],
  "line2_text": "...",
  "word_count": n,
  "verbs_found": [ ... ],
  "token_overlap_count": n,
  "omitted_attributes": [{ "attribute": "...", "reason": "confidence_below_threshold" }],
  "checks_failed": [ ... ],
  "new_noun_introduced": true|false,
  "fallback_reason": "..."
}
- Log these diagnostics programmatically for every image to permit threshold sweeps and to compute hallucination_count and token_overlap_rate.

Enforcement notes (implementation recommended)
- Many rules are programmatic filters; do not rely solely on the generator to obey soft language cues. Implement a post-generation verifier that:
  1) canonicalizes nouns/attributes in the candidate,
  2) computes detector_confidence and clip_retrieval_freq overlap with Line 1,
  3) rejects any candidate failing hard checks and regenerates/falls back to Option B or "image unclear",
  4) emits diagnostics as above.
- If the model is frozen and cannot be controlled reliably, use a deterministic repair: produce Option B from Line 1 tokens when Option A verification fails.

Short exemplars (illustrative)
- Valid Option A:
Line1: child, motorcycle, red
Line2: a child rides a red motorcycle down the street.
- Valid Option B (fallback):
Line1: dog
Line2: dog on sidewalk
- Image unclear:
Line1:
Line2: image unclear
- Negative example (what to avoid — hallucination fallback):
Wrong generator output: "man sits near bicycle with fruit baskets"
Correct behavior: reject (new noun "fruit baskets" not in Line1) → fallback to Option B, for example:
Line1: man, bicycle
Line2: man near bicycle

Targets to monitor (per-run)
- mean_caption_len, fraction captions >13 words (target: reduce >13 by 95%), token_overlap_rate (>=2 tokens target ≥ 95%), hallucination_rate (new_noun_introduced fraction target < 1–2%), mean_clip, mean_delta_clip, clip_win_rate.

Strictly follow the hard constraints above. If a candidate fails any required check and no valid fallback exists, output exactly: image unclear. Log diagnostics for every attempted candidate to aid tuning and CLIP reranking.

best_record.textgrad_loss_text:
Summary of problems (from the report)
- Overall CLIP alignment is poor: mean_clip = 0.252, mean_delta_clip = -0.074, clip_win_rate = 0.0 — the current prompt/pipe produces captions that score worse than the baseline CLIP targets.
- Captions are too long on average (mean_caption_len = 24.1) and violate the intended 7–13 / 2–4 constraints, so the generator is ignoring or failing the hard checks.
- High hallucination/generic behaviour: generic_rate ≈ 29% and negative deltas on many low-performing examples — the model is either introducing new nouns or using non-discriminative tokens that hurt CLIP similarity.
- SigLIP also falls (secondary metric), confirming the outputs are not better semantically.

Concise, actionable changes (priority ordered)

1) Enforce the hard constraints with a strict post-generation verifier and deterministic repair
   - Implement the verifier to 1) canonicalize all candidate tokens, 2) check word counts, allowed verbs, no-new-nouns, token overlap, punctuation rules, etc., and 3) if any check fails immediately produce Option B (or "image unclear" if Option B impossible).
   - Make the verifier non-optional and central — current numbers strongly indicate it's not being applied.

2) Fix the word-count/format leakage immediately
   - The generator must never output >13 words for Option A or >4 tokens for Option B. If the frozen model cannot be trusted, always generate a deterministic Option B from Line 1 tokens.
   - This will reduce mean_caption_len and reduce hallucinations.

3) Re-weight tag selection to favor CLIP-preferred surface forms
   - Current 0.6*det_conf + 0.4*clip_freq seems to pick detector-first tokens that CLIP does not prefer. Sweep toward higher CLIP weight (e.g., detector: 0.4, clip_freq: 0.6) and measure mean_delta_clip.
   - Also when canonical_id has multiple surface forms, select the surface form with the highest CLIP_retrieval_freq (while preserving canonical mapping).

4) Improve canonicalization and surface-form choice
   - Some logs show canonical mapping (e.g., man→person) but generators then use inconsistent surface forms. Use canonical_id for logic but choose the exact output token that maximizes CLIP retrieval frequency among allowed canonical synonyms.
   - Ensure multiword fused objects are handled properly (e.g., "reception desk" vs "desk") and included if detector and CLIP both favor them.

5) Make Option B the reliable fallback and simplify Option A coverage
   - Because the model is frozen, rely on Option B for high coverage: construct tight 2–4 token phrases using the top Line 1 noun and a high-confidence scene/preposition. Deterministic B will reduce hallucination and increase token_overlap_rate.
   - Only attempt Option A when there are at least two high-confidence nouns and the verifier certifies verb/word-count/overlap constraints.

6) Expand and/or tune the allowed verb list carefully
   - The tiny allowed-verb set may be rejecting many valid captions or causing odd rewrites. Either expand with a small curated set of frequent visible verbs (e.g., talks, sleeps, cooks, stands, sits — but keep it conservative) or remove verb use unless verifier confirms exact mapping to Line 1 tokens.
   - Prefer prepositional Option A (single spatial preposition) when in doubt; spatial relations often yield higher CLIP scores.

7) Attribute handling: loosen threshold but log effects
   - Try lowering attribute_confidence_threshold to 60% (run sweep 60/70/75) and permit attribute inclusion only when both detector_confidence and CLIP_retrieval_freq are high. This often increases specificity and CLIP score.
   - Keep at most one adjective in Line 1, but make selection CLIP-aware.

8) Generate multiple candidates only with an external CLIP reranker
   - To improve mean_clip, the integrator should provide an external CLIP reranker. When available, produce 2–3 candidates derived from alternate top-k Line 1 token sets and rerank by CLIP score.
   - If no reranker, strictly produce one candidate.

9) Logging & diagnostics: make the per-candidate JSON mandatory and comprehensive
   - The diagnostics block is essential for tuning. Ensure it always includes clip_retrieval_freq, detector_confidence, checks_failed, new_noun_introduced, and fallback_reason. Use these logs to compute hallucination_rate and token_overlap_rate automatically.

10) Quick tuning knobs to try now
   - Tag ordering weight: clip_freq 0.6 / detector 0.4 (instead of current 0.4/0.6).
   - attribute_confidence_threshold: sweep {60, 70, 75}.
   - tie_break_delta_confidence: try tightening from 10% → 5% for clearer ties.
   - preferred_tag_count: keep 3 when available but evaluate lowering to 2 for scenes with ambiguous small objects (reduces generators introducing irrelevant nouns).

Examples of likely root causes (diagnostic pointers)
- Generator is producing long generic sentences because post-generation checks are not enforced.
- Canonical mapping is applied, but the surface form chosen is not the one CLIP expects, lowering similarity.
- The model introduces nouns/attributes not in Line 1 (hallucinations) because the generator has freedom and no reject-or-fallback step is enforced.

Minimal prioritized checklist to implement now (what will most quickly raise mean_clip)
1. Add/enable strict post-generation verifier + deterministic fallback to Option B.
2. Reduce mean caption length by enforcing the 7–13 / 2–4 hard limits programmatically.
3. Re-weight tag ranking to favor CLIP_retrieval_freq (try 0.4/0.6 det/CLIP) and pick surface forms favored by CLIP.
